title: Excellent tick list tracker
body: I have been using everyday for over a year, and find it the best tick list tracker I’ve used, and I’ve used a lot of them.  I bought the lifelong subscription I like it so much.  It makes me feel like a winner as it tallies all my successes at the top of each page.  The color coding is motivating and the ability to schedule which days to do what and have allowed skips to keep your streak is smart as it’s dealing with real people with real lives.  It’s easy to use on my iPad, iPhone and Apple Watch.  I also can set tasks for a time period, reach my goal and archive them, which I can then reactivate again another time, which is great for seasonal habits.  The psychology behind the app of building habits to support achieving goals is well founded and works.  If you’re serious about your self-growth, this is a great app.  Since it has a free tier, it is worth giving it a go to see if it works for you.  It’s a surprisingly powerful app with a simple intuitive interface.  Thank you for creating it!

title: Good but absurdly expensive
body:
Everyday is a good habit tracker — it has good widgets, a good streak concept that genuinely motivates me and is rather simplistic.

All this made it disappointing when I found out about this apps pricing. A subscription model for an app like this is completely unnecessary, 30€ a year for a good but very simple app is not fair. It gets even more ridiculous when you consider it costs 99€ to purchase this app for life.

If you don’t want to submit to the genuinely absurd pricing then you are limited to tracking only 3 habits. Which by the way makes many widgets appear broken as they tend to have a multiple of 4 rows. 

All in all I would recommend to stay clear from this app, not only because short of spending an absurd amount of money it falls very short of what potential it has, but also to avoid supporting horrible business practices like this.

Finally, it’s just an habit tracking app, it’s good but far from groundbreaking. There’s tons of better options out there.

title: So far so not sure
body: I really like the idea and the beautiful look of the app, but the quality and devil is in the details, and the app has some way to go. The first thing I notice is that when I am to make a password, they only ask me to enter it once and I cannot see what I have written. Let’s just hope that I wrote what I thought I did, for the next time I am to login. Then, when I click “+ make new habit”, everything is filled in with my previous habit. I think I am editing my old one, so I click Cancel and try again. The same thing 4-5 times before I finally try to wipe out (there is no x to remove all the previous text either), and enter a new goal specifics on every line. It turns out this was how it should be done. Very non-intuitive. Also, whenever I click to write on a new line, it doesn’t capitalize the First letter which is annoying when you are to look at the habit name every day so I have to go back and Write properly. The UI looks a bit messy with large links to some videos (with some weird names?), other links are small. Basically, I ended up purchasing this to try for a year because I like the concept and the Black Friday deal (which right now is 15 euro, or 1 euro a month as they say - because details are not important and they clearly live in a 15 month year!) but for the price they are charging for this app, I really think they should have a quality control and think more about their user interface. Just follow the standards you see in other apps and you will be well on your way. I hope my monitary contribution will help them become better. And I hope I will become a better self by using this app every day. Win win?

title: Premium Prices r baddd
body:
The app is small and only has a little over 500 reviews at the moment.

 Having premium prices this heavy are wrong when the app is that small and not well known. If you want the app to expand, the premium needs to be cheaper or people like myself won’t buy into the app as much as we like it.

- $9.99 a month
- $39.99 per year
- $129.99 life time

Respectfully, the prices are not anywhere close to worth it considering what the premium offers… not saying the premium isn’t good but at those prices it can’t be considered. For example, there are annual plans out there for other apps that are a decent chunk cheaper and offer way more features and functionality for the user. 

Usually on other habit/productivity apps there are subscription slashes on ALL premium plans on special days like new years and even student discounts which I think could be offered to incentivize more people to download this app and help spread the word out!

The app is good but these are just my 2 cents considering the current state of premium subscriptions. Will come back to the app & update my review if anything changes.

title: Good, simple, straightforward
body:
I was inspired to try habit formation by a good friend of mine who introduced me to Seinfeld’s X effect. We normally would make giant poster grids with the largest markers we could find at the craft store. The dopamine hit for crossing out a day where a habit was successfully completed was a really satisfying end to the day. Sadly I moved away from my old town, and I haven’t really had much interest in hanging a big poster in my room that I share with my partner.

Everyday fits the bill for this in many ways. It synchronizes really well, it’s much more discreet than the giant posters, and it is VERY easy to document progress. My one, and only, complaint is that it doesn’t have the same dopamine hit as the posters. It’s close with the flash the icons do once they’re tapped, but something more extreme would be greatly appreciated.

body:
I really loved this app when I first got it. But after over a month of using I had to switch to the Done app instead. With everyday you can’t see on a calendar which days you did or didn’t complete. You can only go back so far and then it just vanishes. I can’t view my inputted selections from January. Which is really unfortunate since I paid for the yearly membership. And at $40 that’s a steep price to pay for your information to just vanish. I would have preferred to be able to see on a calendar view my progress. Now I’ve paid and I’ve switch to a different developer who can meet the needs I want. And at a significantly lower cost too. $25 for the years and it includes SIX different habit forming apps. 
I wish I could support this app as the colour aspect was what drew me to it. But sadly it’s lacking more.
Response to your reply it does not tell you on a calendar view I mark things off on my calendar as well and when I looked at that block view it didn’t not add up correctly per day going backwards. Your app is lacking in a lot of areas. Take a look at the done app and see just how many features you’re missing. I’m out $40 now for your app that I’ve now deleted cause it’s useless to me but yet Done app gave me SIX different apps full feature for only $25 for the year. You need to rethink you’re extremely overpriced app for a bunch of coloured blocks.
EDIT #2. Maybe because I’m out $40 for an app that only colours squares and doesn’t even track them properly for history. Your history view is WRONG and does not align with my calendar. You’re robbing people. $40 is a damn joke. You should be ashamed of yourself.

title: Great interface and contents
body:
I love how easy it is to gauge every habit organized in one place. Also, the analytical feature is really helpful. Motivating contents are great and I prefer the resources Everyday gives than meditating fictional stories from some other apps. It is just my own preference. 

I’ve tried other popular habit apps yet decide to pick this one and delete the others. 

However, if there is some feedback I could give, it would be to add a time log feature. I find myself not having the patience to track down the time duration of each activity I do. I set habit as hours put in, for example: 30’ reading books. It would be nice at the end of month to know how many hours did I invest in a particular habit, or how many percentage did I really stick to that goal. 

If I can just nitpick one more thing, it is the difficulty to click backwards after I view resources. I had to press many times or press hard somehow. 

Thank you for creating this app. Thanks for spending the time reading my long review as well. Wish you the best!

title: perfect!
body:
This is such a user-friendly, and all in all friendly, app! 

It's simple and straight to the point, there's instructions...
During the first seven days, you'll be receiving (encouraging) emails, I loved that! 
You can turn them off if you don't like it though, which I think is another great point.

If you don't get the premium version, you can only track 3 habits at a time, but it is enough to get started and once you've created a habit out of something, you don't need to track it anymore, so you can switch it to something else/new!

The developers did a fantastic job.

title: 是我一直想要的记录形式！
body: 这样类似表格的记录形式，我真的找了很久，特别好 很符合我的心意。现在太多习惯养成、时间计划、待办事项的app，但大部分都是关注具体的某一天，以任务清单的形式呈现。但是如果这些习惯都转化为每天的任务，看起来特别繁琐，给人一种一天的任务量繁重的心理感受。我之前就尝试过自己做这样的习惯表格，形式和everyday类似，纵轴是习惯、横轴是日期，可以特别直观地观察到完成情况。没想到真的有这样的app，简约易用感觉开发者也特别有诚意，很满意了。但还是有希望能改进的地方：每天的任务完成只能表示已完成和跳过，能否加入一个备注功能呢，使用者可以写一下这个习惯的完成情况，如果跳过也可以写一下请假理由等等，这样或许会让每天的记录变得更有趣。

title: Great visual tracking, needs better weekly habit support
body: Great app for visual habit tracking and staying motivated. However, it needs better support for habits that are done only a few times per week or once a week. The visual consistency is what makes habit tracking motivating, and preserving that harmony is more important than the streak number itself.

title: Feedback
body:
Hi Joan,

First of all, I want to say I really enjoy using your app—it’s been a valuable tool for staying on top of my habits, and I truly appreciate the thought and effort behind it.

I wanted to share two suggestions that I believe could make the experience even better:
	1.	Widget Tinting (iOS 18): With iOS 18, it’s now possible to tint app icons and widgets to better match the home screen background. Currently, the widgets from your app don’t seem to support this feature. Would it be possible to update them to allow for color customization? It would really help with visual consistency and personalization.

	2.	Grouping Habits into Sections: It 
would also be great to have a way to organize habits into sections with headlines—such as Health, Social, or specific goals. This would give a clearer overview and help visually connect habits to larger targets or areas of life.

Thanks again for all the great work on the app. I’m a big fan and looking forward to seeing how it continues to evolve!

Best regards,
Lorenz

title: genauso das wonach ich gesucht habe!
body: Das ist meiner Meinung nach die beste App um seine Gewohnheiten einfach und übersichtlich zu tracken. Vor allem gefällt mir die Statistik und die sich daraus ergebende Erfolgsrate, die mich total motiviert weiter zu machen! Nun das, was mir nicht gefällt: ich als Ersteller würde mir das mit den Abopreisen anders überlegen. Ich persönlich mag dieses Abo-System nicht und will nicht mehrere Jahre 30€ pro Jahr „nur“ für einen Habit-Tracker zahlen. Ich verstehe natürlich, dass es für den Entwickler auch nicht so einfach ist und das Geld irgendwo her muss, um weiter an Verbesserung der App zu arbeiten. Ich glaube aber es wäre besser, wenn man die Premium-Version einmalig zu einem vernünftigen Preis kaufen könnte.

title: Precio excesivo
body:

Y ahora viene el pero, según la estaba configurando la app viene limitada su versión gratuita a 4 hábitos (me parecen muy pocos), cuando la misma app te explicita que tienes que ser concreto con los hábitos alentándote a crear más para que realmente sea efectivo, de modo que esos 4 hábitos quedan en nada y el precio si es que la quieres pagar son más de 7€ al mes! Una pena la verdad, según la instale, la desinstale.

title: Enhorabuena al desarrollador
body:
Existen muchos motivos por la que recomiendo esta aplicación. Si buscas una app para registrar tus objetivos y hacer un seguimiento de tus hábitos estás en el sitio adecuado.

Lo que más me ha gustado es su minimalismo y su fa idas de uso (solo te llevará tres minutos para saber usar la app). Además he aprendido muchos consejos de los correos electrónicos que me llegan. Creo que el equipo cuida muy bien esos detalles. 

Por otro lado, cabe destacar que es multiplataforma. Con tu cuenta puedes acceder a tu perfil de objetivos en cualquier dispositivo (incluido la versión web en caso de que no puedas descargar la app).

Gracias por la aplicación (5 de 5).

title: Ma vie a changé
body:
L’application dont je ne pensais pas avoir besoin … je suis une personne ayant des objectifs ambitieux mais qui bifurque facilement à droite à gauche, des difficultés à rester accrocher à un projet et des difficultés à être constant sur le long terme. En bref je commence pleins de choses mais je ne concrétise rien …

Everyday me permet de rester fixer à mon objectif en le faisant chaque jour. 30 jours sont passés et j’ai effectivement créé l’habitude de faire un peu de Blender chaque jour (le temps passé chaque jour est en fonction de mes envies et des contraintes de ma journée, mais l’important c’est que je le fais chaque jour !) Résultat : 62h d’expérience accumulés en 30 jours.

Sans la philosophie de cette application, je me serai cramé dès le premier jour a vouloir en faire trop dès le début. Je pense que les habitudes permettent la discipline, et la discipline permet de devenir meilleur dans ce que l’on souhaite, en bref, vous devez installer Everyday !

title: HABIT your way 😉
body:
really unique concept, and cleverly encourages long term habit forming. however, there are a couple of things i would tweak - i think there should be a distinction between ‘failed’ days and days with no data inputted - i sometimes forget whether i’ve remembered to fill in a habit on a day, and to have separate visual cues for each of these conditions would be super helpful. maybe just an X in the box for a failed day and fully blank for ‘no data’?

another thing is the organisation of the widgets - currently, the widget displays the most recent data at the top left, and previous days follows this left to right and descending. I find this (maybe as an english reader) confusing to decipher, and it would make more sense to have the earliest data starting at the top left, and descending from there - perhaps with the ability to scroll up and down once the days overflow the bounds of the widget’s grid…

all in all a well executed app that artfully fulfils its purpose. these few changes, for me, would make the experience even more informative at a glance, especially as a widget user. more colours would be lovely as well (2-colour gradients?!) 

cheers :)

title: Costosa
body:
Allora l’app è comoda e intuitiva. Però dai, troppo costosa! 5 euro al mese non mi sembra proprio il caso. Non credo che il modello di business per quest’app sia un abbonamento. Assolutamente. Se pensare che con 3 euro al mese ci pago 200gb su iCloud o con 10 euro al mese ci pago il pacchetto Office. Dai siamo proprio fuori mercato. Peccato

Aggiornamento 1: si va bene che sei uno sviluppatore indipendente. Però qui stiamo parlando di business. Non puoi dire a un utente una cosa del genere. L’utente fa dei confronti con quello che gli offre il mercato e trae le proprie conclusioni. La tua applicazione è costosa. Quella gratuita è troppo limitata. 

Consiglio per il futuro: prova ad offrire più abitudini e a limitare qualcos’altro. In questo modo l’utente può davvero utilizzare l’app, si affezionerà e si abbonerà anche. Nelle condizioni odierne con sole 3 abitudini non è possibile testare l’app dovrei abbonarmi prima ancora di provarla. E questa cosa non va bene.

title: Ottimo strumento di autoproduttività
body:
Chi di noi non si è mai lanciato a sognare progetti favolosi, magari anche geniali, ma che poi si arenano pian piano nelle sabbie delle altre preoccupazioni quotidiane?

Everyday è una app semplice per un principio semplice: non si realizzano grandi cose in una sola ora di santa ispirazione, ma lavorando con disciplina, tutti i giorni, pagina per pagina fino ad arrivare a fare del proprio progetto una vera success story.

Basta la app per riuscirci? Ovviamente no, tenacia e perseveranza non si vendono sull’apple store. Ma everyday aiuta a tenere traccia dei propri progressi e della propria implicazione, vedere a quali si è fedeli e quali invece finiscono sempre procrastinati.
Magari aiuta a scegliere, o a continuare.

Certamente aiuta.

title: App on life-support which can be vibe-coded has no business to have subscription and those prices
body:
This is, while pleasant, is just quite minimal, basic and finished app on life-support with quite simple functionality. This is not a live service, not some advanced tool. It’s rarely updates while adding nothing new for years - and it has the subscription for that and “lifetime” access costs $60(or 99 internationally!), seriously? What are you ask us to pay for when this app is identical to how it was like 5+ years ago when I first used it? Stick to free version people.

UPD: also author’s salty response sees “hate” which doesn’t exists and TOTALLY misses the point. Also some remarks are just strange:

"if you do feel this app can be vibecoded in a weekend...” - bro this is colored habit tracker, extremely popular app category, maybe only todo lists will be easier to code with AI now

And this “AI… benefits from code people like me have shared...”: in author’s GitHub the most starred repo with a code was updated 10+ years ago, just fyi for those ppl reading it

title: Есть куда развиваться
body: Все отлично. Позволю себе пару предложений: 1). День  с невыполненной привычкой должен отличаться от дня, когда этой привычки еще нет. Например, решение - ежедневно бегать с понедельника, которое не выполнено. Тогда понедельник на табло должен отличаться от воскресенья. Соответственно, TOTAL COUNT в конце недели (если больше фейлов не было) должен быть не 100%, а 86% (6 из 7) Это важно, т. к. исключает уязвимость мотивации на старте: "Не получилось сегодня - не страшно, начну завтра". 2). Сделайте отдельно режим просмотра и режим редактирования для табло. Чтобы не было случайных тапов при его сдвигании.

title: Очень нравится, но не хватает разнообразия цветов
body: Безумно нравится приложение, очень удобно, без лишней фигни (которую обычно любят добавлять в подобные приложения), минималистично, все интуитивно понятно, есть расширенная статистика, очень удобный виджет, где можно сразу отметить выполнение, и именно такое приложение с рабочим виджетом я и искала! Не везде можно одним тыком с экрана домой отметить привычки, не нужно каждый раз заходить в приложение, я добавила смарт-папку и объединила несколько виджетов с привычками по группам (кстати можно выбрать какие привычки отражаются в виджете), и это так просто и удобно! Я в восторге! Цена очень адекватная, если брать подписку на год, огромное спасибо разработчику за его старание и такую хорошую цену! title: 簡單、直覺、實用
body:
對於想要長期培養習慣，但懶得自己畫格子或影印各種paper的人來說，是一個非常實用的app，而且數據可以被儲存，也可以在電腦跟手機之間同步，對於我這種常常把紙本紀錄弄不見的人來說，真的是福音。

另外習慣（或是戒斷壞習慣）的呈現方式都很直覺，讓使用者可以依據顏色深淺就判斷自己這個習慣現在大概持續多久了。skip的功能也很人性化，畢竟偶爾還是會想偷懶兩天。

唯一美中不足的大概就是顏色有點少，對於使用到後期有很多習慣的我來說，有點不夠用，希望開發者可以改善這個問題。

但是瑕不掩瑜，整體來說這還是一個很棒的app，我自己很推薦，也會一直持續使用。

title: What a mess with widgets..
body:
BUGS APPEARING, BEING FIXED, APPEARING AGAIN. Description below. Watch widget is presented as interactive - not just an icon to launch an app, but in fact they are just different skins of a shortcut. Disappointed as I searched for a convenient and interactive watch interface. UPD as requested by developer: ATracker and Flat Tomato are two interactive I can remember at the moment. By “interactive” I mean that they depict regularly updated data. And two of available options for your app imitate the depiction of variable info (say, progress through the day - rounded scale with a number of how many habits are done today, or round scale with countdown, how many left to do - it always shows 6 ), but they do not work. They either require 10 habits to be active (I had 1-3), or they are just icons, variations of shortcut. UPD2: maybe the issue was with particular watchfaces, or the fix was implemented, but now, with different face, it works.
UPD3: widget is missing again. Doesn’t show on my watch (daily to do and one of daily reports). Deleting the app.

title: Simple app, nice features, very easy to follow through with
body:
You can only make three Habits at a time without paying, and yall have LOST your minds if you think I’m about to pay $99 for such basic functionality. 

That said, I think the limit is beneficial since it kept me from piling expectations onto myself. The process is simple enough that it’s never been overwhelming.

My favorite feature is that you can mark a “null” day, which doesn’t add to OR interrupt a streak. It’s nice for when one of my goals wasn’t possible that day, but I don’t want to let go of my streak. Having this in-between makes it so I never feel the need to lie (which is a quick way to lose motivation).

The visual feedback of marking a completed a habit is nice, especially with the bright colors. Your phone also makes a nice *click* vibration which I like. 
You can also view statistics for how often you follow through with your goals. No ads, and an account isn’t required, which is always a plus.

Overall, very satisfied

title: Give this smaller app a chance
body:
I’ve tried a lot of habit trackers, but there is almost always TOO much to fill in that it made me not want to use them. The process of filling everything in felt like it needed to be a habit in itself. 

My ADHD brain gets too distracted; I desperately wanted simplicity. After years, I’ve developed some great habits simply by using timers and reading Atomic Habits, which this app draws some concepts from. Now, I want to visualize this in a simple, easy-understand-visual for novice data folks like my wife or friends. So I turned to this app, (shout out r/dataisbeautiful). This app does just that. With intention and time, I’m excited to see what my visual will look like. Literally 3 click options:

-Did you do it? Tap.
-Did you do some of it? Tap.  Tap.
-Didn’t do it? Tap. Tap. Tap.

Obviously, there are things to fill out. But compared to others, IMO, set up is simple. Reminder options are available. There is even an option for breaking habits! 

Free to use, so I’ve testing with 3 habits and I’m very happy so far. It’s only 1/2, but so far, so good. 

Some improvements for this app, for me, would just be customizable user preferences. Specifically, visuals with fonts. I have unique reading needs so the ability to alter these helps a ton! This would help keep the app accessible for all. TY for your great app.

title: This app helped me change my life
body: When I came to realize that habits are one of the fundamental building blocks of achieving success on the vision I have for my life, my next thought was to find the best system for motivating me to do all my goals every day. I really struggle with consistency, but it’s precisely that lack of consistency that is the #1 limiting factor to me achieving my vision for my life. So I went looking for a habit tracking app that really nails the dopamine reward cycle and would help me be the most motivated and therefore consistent with my daily goals. In short: that app is Everyday. I encourage you to try it for free with just three goals, and once you realize like I did how valuable it is, then shell out the few bucks for the premium version. Best ROI on your money of pretty much anything in life I can think of. This app is really robust; the features for how you can set up your habits covers absolutely everything that you could want to track, and they have icons and visuals and the whole main screen is basically a visualization of how consistent you are becoming. And they’re leveraging gamification things to make it more effective. It’s truly the perfect app for this. Can’t recommend it more.

title: Good but missing some features I'd like...
body:
I have been searching for a visual tracking app like this for ages. I love the color and how it lets you see so many days/habits at once. There are a couple features I would like though.

1. Is there a way to reorded the way the habits appear in the list? For example, the first habit I made was 'code 10 mins' with a reminder at 1700. But then I made 'yoga 20 mins' with a reminder at 700. I wanted to reorder the habits so they appear in the list chornologically, but was unable to do so. My OCD got the better of me and I ended up deleting the first habit because I couldn't take them being out of order.

2. More color options! Or maybe sets? Like a pastels option. Or a neon options. I would totally splurge a buck 99 for a rain themed color pallete, or something seasonal and dumb.

3. A lower life time purchase price. I usually buy the lifetime option if I know I am going to use an app daily. But 99 dollars is pretty steep, so I ended up going for the yearly subscription. 69.99 and I probably would have paid if I liked the weekly trial (and it had some of the features I mentioned above.) Then you can make extra by releasing fun cosmetic stuff like color palettes, etc. People who are choosing your app are probably choosing it for the ascetics, so I'm sure you could make extra cash that way once you have lifetime subscribers.

All in all hopeful for more updates! This is the only visual habit tracker I've found. I was considering making my own!

title: Easily the Simplest Habit Tracking App
body:
This is literally the best app. There’s no fancy stuff here. Just a straightforward, beautifully designed interface for tracking your habits. You can set a time for each habit, or you can forego that option. And you can use their awesome color-coding system to categorize visually the different kinds of habits you want to tackle. 

For instance, for the bad habits I want to say I was able successfully to avoid, I use a forbidding RED. But for habits that connect to my value of Faith (like prayer and scripture reading), I use BLUE. For exercises like pushups: YELLOW, etc.

You get three habits with the free option. For the paid, you can track as many habits as you want. I paid $30 for the year, and I’m not disappointed. I will pay the lifetime $99 subscription if at the end of the year I’m as deeply satisfied as I am now.

Best app this guy has purchased, next to the Dwell app.

title: I recommend this habit tracker all the time
body: In the past I haven’t had any success with habit trackers. I have ADHD and most of them held my attention for a day or two, maybe a week, then I would miss some days, I would feel super guilty, and I didn’t want to open the app again. I’ve used this habit tracker for a year and counting, and I really don’t know why it is so different. It could be the ability to still ‘log’ the days you don’t do something. Instead of filling in the rectangle, it puts a triangle in that space, and that feels like neutral data instead of a personal failing. With this app I found out that I exercised 60% of the time, wrote 80% of the time, never went more than three days without flossing, and I have a ‘high energy’ day WAY more often than I think. In fact, I think this app allows me to live up to my values, because I can provide myself with regular proof—I am the person I want to be.

title: Great BUT WAAAAY OVERPRICED
body:
I love this app and have been using it for years! Unfortunately, it went from $12/year to $3/month to $5/month and now it’s almost $8/month and $30/year. This extra price hike is most likely going to cause me to stop using it since it is a relatively simple app that I can’t justify paying more for than other apps that offer significantly more (even Discovery+ is only $4.99/month!). This is creeping up to be the cost of iTunes and compared to other apps, it’s no longer worth it for a simple app that is essentially a daily habit/to do list. Personally, I love the simplicity and it has been my favorite habit tracker but now that it’s more than “a cup of coffee”, it no longer seems like a fair price to be asking people to pay. I am certain that you’ll see more and more reviews like this one with your most recent price increase and will most likely end up losing customers.

If I could make a suggestion, please go back to $5/month (which I’ve been willing to pay) or make it a one time $30 lifetime cost which I’m sure many people will gladly pay. However, asking for almost $100 for lifetime is GREEDY and UNBELIEVABLE.

So far, this is my favorite app. I only have one issue that could potentially be a deal breaker for me. I’m a shift worker and don’t always know which days I’ll be able to perform a specific task. If there was a way to select a habit for a number of times per week without having to select particular days, I would be sold. title: Great tool for investigating what works
body: A great piece of advice I got: If you want to change a habit, track a habit. I am always tinkering with my scattered mind and i typically feel I have trouble with “self-discipline.” Sometimes “discipline” can trigger resistance, whereas creative reframing of goals, and a gentle attitude toward purse and our challenges can lead to changes we want. I use a lot of different tools for these experiments, and I really appreciate the care and attention that has gone into this app. I’m not always good at using it, but even if I’m only using it for a few months at a time, it’s really helpful in tracking what I can do easily, what I have resistance to, and what seems actually close to impossible. Then I can reevaluate and reset my goals. Worth a look, as long as you don’t stress yourself out with it! It should be part of your kind exploration of your own patterns.

title: I use this app every day. A couple asks for the dev…
body: I love this app. I use it every single day multiple times a day and have for years now. This app has helped me better my mental health and executive function and also is just fun to use. I’m tracking 21 habits now. A couple asks for the developer: I would love very much to have the option to enter a hex code to further customize the colors of all my habits. I will pay for this feature!! It would be really aesthetically pleasing to get more specific with the habit colors, either fully customizable RGB or just a broader color palette would be great. I’d also love to see the total number of weeks for which I’ve tracked a habit and I’d like to be able to zoom out to see all my habits in one screen, even if they’re really small bc I’m tracking a bunch. Thanks so much for making this awesome app. It really is a big part of my daily routine. Thank you for considering this feedback!!

title: Greedy Ludicrous Pricing
body:
If you care about helping the most people possible and doing the most good possible, consider charging what most people will actually pay for a habit app. What’s more important, you making as much money as you can, or you making a bigger impact on the world and uplifting the collective quality of life on earth? Please consider. Thank you for making the app but it is unusable for me at this price range. $100 for a lifetime purchase. For an app that shows a colored tile when I click it? There’s so much more capable software people can buy for $100. Please consider this!

After reading other developer responses it seems the developer does want to help as many people as possible but is having trouble financing their ability to work in coding. 

Is there another solution besides jacking up the price of this 1 app to such high heights?

If you kept the features of this app the same and didn’t work much on it, your work-to-compensation ratio would even out over time even with the app at a lower price point. 

This would free you up to work on other apps/projects. 

If you only want to work on this project and see it as more of a luxury habit-tracking app that caters to richer customers, then alright, I guess I understand. There’s other reasonably priced habit-tracking apps we can use. 

I just have a problem with how many developers are going to subscription model to bleed customers of their money. It’s insane. Almost everything is a subscription now. And it’s not because it’s truly necessary. There’s so much greed now in software. 

There has to be another better way. 

By the way, if 100 different apps & services are trying to charge us the price of a coffee a month, what does that add up to? EVERYONE is trying to do it now.

title: My Most-Used App!
body: I am now on day seven of using this gorgeous habit tracker, and I love it. The colors are pretty, and I find watching the streaks build very motivating. it syncs flawlessly -- and immediately -- across Chrome, iPhone, and Mac. (I haven't tried it on my watch yet.) I found out it could be set up to open in a fresh tab on Chrome, and it's the best thing ever because I am so frequently reminded of my daily habits and able to easily check them off when I'm ready. The week-long starter email series is very helpful, and the "Learn" tab has a wealth of information on setting and maintaining habits, with lots of scientific background about what works and why. I also had a question for the developer, and she got back to me quickly with a kind, helpful email. In the meantime, I had figured out how to solve the issue, but she mentioned that she would keep playing around with it so that others didn't have the same confusion. As a tip, if you change the colors a lot (as I do, since mine are in rainbow order, so I have to tweak things every time I move/add/archive a habit), the easiest way to do it is via the Chrome extension: hover over the habit name, then click on the color dot to the left and choose a new color.) After all, the beauty is part of the point of the app! (Developer: It would be great if it were this easy to change colors on the Mac app, but this is a good work-around and certainly not a deal-breaker!)

title: You may waste a lot of time with this one.
body: Free - with in-app purchases.  Not too long ago, it seems, that generally meant you’d get a highly functional app, maybe 75% of all functions, then if you wanted the other 25%, you could get that via an in-app purchase.  Sadly, that’s not the case with this app, and many others these days.  Here you get very little functionality, not even enough to evaluate if it’s suitable for your purposes, IMO. By the time you discover that you can only track 3 habits with the free version, you’ve already spent 20 minutes or more setting it up.  Now you need to spend an equal amount of time removing all the stuff you installed to remove it completely.  Apple really needs to do something about developers using “Free - with in-app purchases” this way.

The consistency is making a tangible difference in my work, marriage, health, and social life already. Excited to see how long my current streaks on my habits last. title: Great App, Too Expensive
body:
The move to subscriptions has made developers greedy.  I don't want to sound like a jerk, but apps like this are not worth $30/year forever.  That's ABSURD.  I am happy to pay a REASONABLE subscription rate for an app.  Take Deliveries, for example.  Arguably, it's a much more complex app to code and maintain, yet the developer only charges $4.99 PER YEAR.  That is more than fair.  Compare to 1Password.  Everyday is basically the same price!  Absurd!!!  1Password is a far more complex app with a whole development and support team behind it.

All of that said, Everyday is a nice app.  It's intuitive with great use of color, making it both easy to read and visually appealing.  I've had a few email exchanges with the developer and he is friendly and responsive.  I'd pay for the app if it were reasonably priced, but out of principal more than anything else, I refuse to subscribe at these prices.

*Response to the developer:  I agree with what you wrote regarding value.  So let's compare apples to apples.  Awesome Habits is $22.99 for a LIFETIME license.  Habit Tracker (by Davetech Co) is $4.99 for a LIFETIME license.  Each of these apps offers more features than Everyday.  Again, I'm not trying to be a jerk, but $30/year forever is ridiculous.

title: Visually compelling and wonderfully executed
body:
I’ve tried numerous habit trackers and reminder apps over the years, and nothing has grabbed me so completely as this one. The visuals, the clean interface, the gentle reminders to not skip two days (but no “punishment” other than a break in the color gradient if you need to skip twice), the incredibly compelling and nuanced widget options— all of this earns a “wow” from me. I’m historically resistant to subscriptions, but $29/year for what this app is giving me in terms of mental health is an absolute steal. 

Yes, you could do this on paper, but will you? You could do this in a spreadsheet, but will you? Having the large widget right there on my Home Screen has been motivating in a way I have honestly never felt. If you have ADHD this is a jolt to the system in the best possible way. If you’re an artist or designer you’ll love the aesthetic. If you simply need an easy way to track a few habits, go with the free version, it’s marvelous and without ads or other shackles. If you need more than three habits, great! The paid version is well worth the subscription, and I’m glad to be putting money in a skilled independent developer’s hands. Thank you Joan!

title: Developer jacked up the prices
body:
Price went from $1/month to $5/month, or from $12/year to $30/year. Most of the “worth it” reviews reflect the original pricing. No clue why the developer suddenly felt the app was worth 3x the price, and moreover, I’m just sad that apps that once went for a one time purchase of $3 to $5 are now trying to charge the same monthly. I blame Apple for that... greedy!

UPDATE: Developer responded below that the price had to go to because the app wasn’t sustainable. That’s the problem with many app developers today. They want to write one app, get customers, then raise the price. They’ve given up on making other apps and adding more value to draw in more customers. Instead, they’re exploiting their one success story and raising prices for the few who are willing to stick around. It’s happening over and over and over. $4 calendar utilities turning into $20 calendar utilities for a “polish” upgrade, turning into $30/year subscriptions - for a calendar utility.

At the end of the day, if you feel like an app that replicates what you can do with a spreadsheet is worth $60/year, go for it. But this sort of price jacking is ruining the App Store, slowly, through attrition. Maybe the balance sheets don’t yet reflect it, but they will.

The setup allows for “don’t skip twice” mentality which I find is a lot more sustainable than a “don’t break the chain/streaks mean everything” mentality that I see on some self-improvement apps.

title: Love it!
body: These habit tracker apps are great, because once you build up some momentum doing your habits every day, it becomes easier and easier to keep them up. I used to use a different one, but what I love about this one is that I can customize the colors so much, and it maintains a high score, so even if I “break the chain,” I have a goal to start shooting for again right away.

title: Love the app

author: Eightb1666

title: The only habit tracker that works for me.
body:
Everyday is beautifully designed. From the icons, to the simplistic UI, to the subtle color changes, it makes the experience easier to use.

Having a chrome extension in addition to the iPhone app is what allows me to consistently remind me of the important habits to complete each day. 

This app succeed where other streaks app fails for its simplicity and design. You have low over head, one click completion, and easy on the eyes. 

Worth the subscription for me.
